questions.q: At what level is almost every Expenses setup object (templates, policies, audit rules) defined?
options: Once globally for the entire company
questions.explain: Expenses setup objects are scoped per business unit so different parts of a company can have different rules, currencies, and policies.

questions.q: Which setup object must exist before any employee can enter an expense item at all?
questions.explain: No employee can enter an expense item without a template, since templates are the container that expense types sit inside.

questions.q: Why do audit rules have to be set up after expense types and templates, not before?
options: Because there must already be expense types and reports for an audit rule to evaluate against
Audit rules have nothing to do with expense types
Audit rules are optional and never actually required
questions.explain: An audit rule evaluates submitted expense items and reports, so the expense types and templates it checks must already exist.

questions.q: What do expense system options control at the business-unit level?
options: Only the color scheme of the expense entry screen
The company's entire chart of accounts
Receipt requirement thresholds, itemization requirements, default currency, and whether cash advances are allowed
questions.explain: System options are business-unit-level switches covering receipts, itemization, currency defaults, and cash advance availability.

questions.q: In the Castellan Field Services example, what was set up right after the new expense type 'Safety Equipment Rental' was added to its category?
options: A policy limit of $500 without a manager's pre-approval
questions.explain: After adding the expense type to its category, the next step in the example was setting a $500 policy limit requiring pre-approval above that.
